To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Pareto optimality can be characterized by a set of conditions that are sufficient, and also necessary, for the case in which agents have the same number of lives, but not for the more general case.

1) the necessary and sufficient conditions for Pareto efficiency are equivalent when all agents live for a finite number of periods; 2) when agents can live for a finite or an infinite number of periods, the equivalence of necessary and sufficient conditions holds when relative prices satisfy a certain condition; and 3) without the relative prices condition, necessary and sufficient conditions are not equivalent.

in the context of general OLG economies with heterogeneous lifetimes, Pareto optimality requires that (a) the number of agents alive at any point in time be equal to the number of commodities available for consumption, (b) the number of commodities consumed by each agent be the same, and (c) the number of periods of life be equal across all agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: What are the necessary and sufficient conditions for Pareto optimal competitive equilibria to exist in OLG economies?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in a pure exchange OLG economy with heterogeneous lifetimes, a competitive equilibrium is Pareto optimal if and only if relative prices are equal to the ratio between the expected utility from consumption and leisure of two individuals of different ages, and this ratio is the same for any pair of individuals of different ages.
, in general pure exchange OOL economies with heterogeneous lifetimes, Pareto optimality cannot be fully characterized in terms of equilibrium prices.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conditions for Pareto efficiency of a competitive equilibrium are equivalent to the existence of a competitive equilibrium in a modified economy in which the set of agents has been restricted to those with the maximum number of periods of life.

, in general OLG models, Pareto optimal equilibria are those that satisfy the usual first order conditions for a competitive equilibrium and the condition that all individuals have the same lifetime consumption profile.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, even in a simple setting like the one we consider here, the conditions for Pareto optimal equilibria are very restrictive and hence the set of Pareto optimal equilbria can be small.
in the case in which agents have the same number of life periods, the conditions for Pareto efficiency are much simpler than in the general case.
, in the presence of heterogeneous lifetimes, the characterization of Pareto optima requires more restrictive assumptions on relative prices than in the case of homogeneous lifetimes.
